clue.text: Applaud another part of meaningless nonsense

parts.note: to applaud is to clap

indicators.note: another version of the word part means its letters are rearranged into a different form

explanation.surface: Clapping one more section of something that makes no sense at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' reads like 'one more', but it signals a different arrangement of the word part; 'of' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk designed only to win applause: a synonym for drivel.

clue.text: Tribe with force produced by a loud resounding noise

parts.note: a tribe is a clan
G is the abbreviation for gravitational force, as in g-force

explanation.surface: A tribe forcefully making a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a ringing metallic crash, the kind of loud resonant sound a struck bell makes.

clue.text: A large number hidden by personal assistant found food that was pleasant to taste

indicators.note: something hidden by another is enclosed within it, so these letters sit inside the assistant's

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
table can mean the food served, as in 'keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: An assistant finds a big number of tasty dishes concealed somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a 'large number'; 'found' is only a link. Table meaning the fare served is an old but familiar sense ('keeps a good table').
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable describes food agreeable to the palate, that is, nice to eat.

clue.text: American Indian in so, socialist's family

parts.note: a socialist is a red, here possessive
one's kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A Native American belonging to a left-winger's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RED'S KIN, the socialist's family. The term is now regarded as offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a dated, now offensive, name for a Native American person.

clue.text: Tactless way to test the bathwater

definitions.text: Tactless way to test the bathwater

parts.words: Tactless way to test the bathwater
parts.note: literally dipping a foot into the bath to check its heat, and also the idiom for saying something clumsy

explanation.surface: A clumsy method of checking whether the bath is warm enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to blunder socially, saying something embarrassing; literally it is a foot dipped in water.

clue.text: No gentleman in the CIA can make a loud chirpy sound

definitions.text: can make a loud chirpy sound

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, the cad going inside the intelligence agency

parts.note: the CIA is the American Central Intelligence Agency, kept as written
a cad is a man who behaves badly, no gentleman

explanation.surface: A bounder in the American intelligence agency can make a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition describes the insect by what it does: male cicadas produce a shrill buzzing song.

clue.text: Succeed or fail

definitions.meaning: a plan that comes off works out well
to ... can mean to fall from a horse or bike, or to ... worst

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to work out as planned and to be thrown or lose out.

clue.text: Not the sort of person to go to a dance?

definitions.text: Not the sort of person to go to a dance?

parts.words: Not the sort of person to go to a dance?
parts.note: split after its first letter, the word reads as the article plus a party with dancing, yet the whole means unsociable

explanation.surface: Someone who avoids dances.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding the company of others, the opposite of someone attending social gatherings.

clue.text: Not well used form of transport?

definitions.text: Not well used form of transport?

parts.words: Not well used form of transport?
parts.note: the surface suggests a rarely used vehicle, but it means one used by people who are not well

explanation.surface: A means of travel that few people use.
explanation.definitionFit: This vehicle carries sick or injured people to hospital.

clue.text: Wandered but didn't start, having moved at an easy pace

indicators.note: the word fails to begin, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: to have wandered is to have rambled

explanation.surface: Someone who strolled but never set off.
explanation.definitionFit: To have strolled leisurely; a synonym for walking at a relaxed pace.

clue.text: In due course this device gives a report

definitions.text: In due course this device gives a report

parts.words: In due course this device gives a report
parts.note: report here is a loud bang, made after a set delay

explanation.surface: A gadget that eventually produces a written account.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive set to detonate at a set moment; report is the bang of the blast.

clue.text: Asking to exchange some leather

indicators.note: the letters of the words are swapped about into new positions

explanation.surface: Requesting a swap of a piece of hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather made from the hide of a nanny or billy is a familiar kind.

clue.text: To sail out of a mouth-like opening

indicators.note: out here suggests the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A sailing trip leaving from a harbour mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostial is the adjective from ostium, an anatomical or botanical opening.

clue.text: Surgeon noted skeleton

parts.note: to have noted something is to have seen it
a skeleton is a set of bones

explanation.surface: A doctor observed a skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: This is old slang for a doctor who operates, from the days of amputation.

clue.text: Incidental illustration of what can be found on the front of a car, oddly enough

definitions.meaning: a piece of information shedding indirect light on a subject

definitions.text: what can be found on the front of a car

explanation.surface: An unexpected picture of something on a vehicle's bonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' merely links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an incidental piece of illumination on a matter and a small vehicle lamp.

clue.text: Dropped everyone in the marshy ground

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes inside the word for marsh

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, as in East Anglia
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Everybody let go in the bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallen means having come down or tumbled, the past participle of fall.

clue.text: Rather slowly right in, inside Los Angeles poor quarter

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes within the run of the city and the district

parts.note: a ghetto is a deprived part of a city

explanation.surface: Slow progress inside a deprived district of a Californian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Larghetto is the musical tempo marking meaning fairly slow, a little quicker than largo.

clue.text: Quite good covering up?

definitions.meaning: reasonably satisfactory, as in a respectable effort
suitably dressed so as not to be exposed

explanation.definitionFit: Decent means both fairly satisfactory and clothed enough to be seen.

clue.text: Many a catcall's emanating originally from the kitchen

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
catcalls are boos

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Lots of jeering comes out of the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A caboose is a ship's galley, where food is cooked on board.

clue.text: Slovenly woman to go round inside quietly

indicators.note: the turning word sits within the little word to

parts.note: taken as written
to roll is to go round
P stands for piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A scruffy woman sneaks round indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A trollop is an old term for a slatternly or promiscuous woman.

clue.text: Stubborn old boy expected to surround deserter

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: the word for expected encloses the turncoat

parts.note: something expected is due
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A stubborn former pupil, due to hem in a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means unyieldingly persistent, refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Disguise unwelcome facts in masquerade

definitions.meaning: to present bad news in a more attractive light

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to embellish something to hide its faults and to wear fancy costume.

clue.text: I do, after party, have a vital urge

indicators.note: one piece follows the other in the answer

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: Saying the wedding vows after a celebration, keen for what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I do' comes after LIB, the Liberal Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual drive, one of the basic life instincts.

clue.text: These troubles can make babies feel down in the mouth

definitions.text: These troubles can make babies feel down in the mouth

parts.words: These troubles can make babies feel down in the mouth
parts.note: down in the mouth means glum, but literally new growth in an infant's gums causes discomfort

explanation.surface: Problems that make infants miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies cutting their first teeth are fretful; the soreness is literally in the mouth.

clue.text: The measurement right round

parts.note: a measure taken all the way around a body or object

explanation.surface: Measuring all the way around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is circumference, the distance around a waist or tree trunk.

clue.text: Most of the small round particle in single protein

indicators.note: almost all the word is used, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: a globule is a tiny ball or droplet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of a tiny ball in one kind of protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Globulins are a class of simple proteins found in blood plasma and elsewhere.

clue.text: One not standing up to an easy catch

definitions.meaning: someone seated, or who poses seated for a portrait
in cricket, a chance so simple it should be taken

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a seated person and, in cricket, a dolly chance that is easy to hold.

clue.text: A form of protection to boot

definitions.text: A form of protection to boot

parts.words: A form of protection to boot
parts.note: to boot means in addition, but here a guard fitted to footwear

explanation.surface: An extra safeguard thrown in as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A reinforced cap covering the front of a shoe or boot protects the toes.

clue.text: First-rate spinner, Nick

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy
a nick is a notch

explanation.surface: An excellent slow bowler named Nick.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch means excellent, of the highest quality.
